title: Something you know, or something you have?
instruction: Two-factor authentication combines two different things. Which of these do you know, which do you have, and which isn’t a secret at all?

items.why: You have it in your head or in a password manager.

items.text: A code from the authenticator app on your phone
items.why: It is created only on your phone.

items.text: A security key on your keyring
items.why: A physical thing you carry with you.

items.text: A text-message code sent to your number
items.why: It comes only to your SIM card.
Anyone who visits your profile can see it.

items.text: Your dog’s name, which is in your bio
items.why: What is on your profile is public.

debrief: 2FA protects you because an attacker would need both: what you know and what you have. Public information protects nothing.
